escalations: None required. Two semantics notes for the orchestrator, not decided here. (1) A broad certificate carrying both p-host1 and p-host2 is accepted by both CA hosts, which confirms spec 7.6: per-destination scope exists only through server-side principal mapping. summary: The disposable SSH fixtures under tests/fixtures/ssh/ work. up.sh, smoke.sh, reset.sh and down.sh all ran, and the fixtures are left DOWN. In the final cycle smoke.sh passed 60/60 checks on each of four runs (three consecutive, one after reset.sh with a dirtied registry). down.sh exited 0 with CLEANUP CONFIRMED and zero containers, networks, images or runtime/ left. The base is debian@sha256:f324c7ff...e9ffc4b1, and the containers run openssh-server 1:10.0p1-7+deb13u4 (sshd OpenSSH_10.0p2). The host client is /usr/bin/ssh 10.3p1. Verified scenarios: fixed-auth host with a root-owned registry, the enrollable host (add and remove a marker key, unrelated bytes identical, a concurrent edit preserved), two CA hosts with different principal files, bastion ProxyJump without agent forwarding to an internal-only target, and host-key substitution failing hard. Two findings are worth knowing. A certificate with both principals works on both CA hosts, which confirms the spec 7.6 scope caveat. OpenSSH PerSourcePenalties caused one flaky false failure, so the fixture sshd sets PerSourcePenalties no. Earlier failed attempts (7 faulty checks in smoke.sh, then that flake) are kept as attempt-*.log. tests/fixtures/MANIFEST.md lists every fixture in plan 6.2 with owner, versions, role, reset, cleanup, status and the key-disposal procedure. Windows/WSL and locked-provider fixtures are blocked, and the rest are not_started or implemented_unverified."
